mechanisms.title: Authority Action Propagation
mechanisms.problem: Disarming future goal rounds did not stop a live turn or prevent a later model turn from undoing a durable user pause. Host cancellation, exact attempt fencing and a pre-service model-resume rejection preserve user control without forbidding disarmed-active or blocked continuation.
triggers: A host/user pauses a goal during any live turn, including a non-goal turn, or resumes before its cancelled attempt reaches idle.
A later model update_goal resume encounters a durable paused goal, a restored/forked disarmed-active goal or a blocked goal after human continuation.
obligations: In the round driver, operation=pause with currentInitiator()!=agent aborts any live turn via agent.cancel({kind:'user'},{keepInbox:true}); a model-initiated pause retains its acknowledgement turn.
Preserve pending Inbox work and the existing queued-round reservation refusal after disarm; fence the cancelled idle handler to the attempt's exact goalId/revision so a newer resume is not re-paused.
Reject model update_goal resume of a durable paused goal with GOAL_TOOL_RESUME_PAUSED before calling GoalService, even in a later human turn.
Keep model resume available for disarmed-active goals after restore/fork and blocked goals after human continuation; do not reject every inactive phase.

Durable paused resume is user-owned through Web, /goal resume or another direct goal-service caller. State that ownership in the model prompt and tool description; prompt-only restraint cannot replace the code guard.
steps: The round-driver owner handles host pause using initiator identity and keepInbox, leaving durable state/event ownership in GoalService.
The tool owner checks durable paused status before service resume and returns GOAL_TOOL_RESUME_PAUSED; preserve disarmed-active/blocked paths and document user ownership.
The reviewer checks direct human/domain resume separately from model authority and tests immediate resume against the stale cancelled attempt's exact id/revision.
The regression owner exercises live ordinary and goal turns, queued reservations, later-turn tool refusal and restored/forked/blocked acceptance through the real owners.

enforcement.implementation: Source round-driver cancellation/fencing and the model tool's pre-GoalService paused-resume rejection are automatic effects. Target driver/tool/domain bindings and execution remain missing; this class does not claim that the Skill already supplies that runtime.
enforcement.trust: Host versus agent initiator identity and exact goal id/revision establish authority. User-owned durable pause cannot be lifted by model natural-language continuation; direct domain callers remain distinct from the model tool.
enforcement.failure: Durable paused model resume fails with GOAL_TOOL_RESUME_PAUSED before service side effects; disarmed-active and blocked remain resumable. A stale idle cancellation cannot overwrite a newer revision.
enforcement.exceptions: Model-initiated pause does not abort its acknowledgement. Host abort intentionally covers any live turn, not just a goal round, and retains Inbox. Direct Web/command/service resume remains allowed; durable formats are unchanged.

mechanisms.applicability: Apply where user-owned durable pause and model-accessible resume coexist with live execution. Record actual absence of that domain if untriggered and reactivate on introduction; missing tool/driver integration is an open effect gap, not non-applicability.

migration.strategy: Keep durable state in the domain, host control in the round driver and model authority rejection before the service call.

migration.requiredSupport: Real goal service, live driver and model tool, host/Web or command resume, initiator identity, goal revision and later-turn/restore/fork/blocked controls; target effect proof remains missing.

rejection.scenario: In a later human turn, model update_goal resume of the durable paused goal returns GOAL_TOOL_RESUME_PAUSED and GoalService is not called. Removing the pre-service guard must fail this control; cancelling every model pause and re-pausing a newer revision must fail their acknowledgement/fencing controls.

recovery.scenario: Resume the durable paused goal through the real Web control, /goal resume or authorized direct domain caller; allow its new revision to stay resumed when the old cancelled turn reaches idle. This is user-owned recovery, not model retry of the rejected tool action.

mechanisms.limitations: Human/domain resume is not a grant to model update_goal. Disarmed-active after restore/fork and blocked after human continuation intentionally remain model-resumable. Prompt/tool-description wording cannot enforce the rejection without the guard. mechanisms.title: Bounded Auxiliary State
mechanisms.problem: Resolved-reply backlog does not bound still-awaiting binding closures, and per-data-event counts can be stale before microtasks drain. The CPython host caps true outstanding calls at1024 with one deduplicated setImmediate check per macrotask plus a done-frame re-check; binding metadata is read once into plain values before validation/boot. Cursor metering and mid-drain reply-prefix compaction address separate auxiliary-memory costs.
triggers: A child can issue binding calls faster than unresolved binding promises settle.
Multiple flowing-mode data events arrive within one macrotask, or done shares the flood's batch.
Getter-backed binding metadata is validated before later boot serialization, or wide completion/reply draining retains excessive auxiliary state.
obligations: Count pendingCalls before dispatch and release in finally on all reply/rejection/settled-drop exits; allow exactly1024 outstanding calls, reject strictly greater as worker-exit with call-backlog diagnostic.

Schedule one deduplicated setImmediate check after the macrotask's microtasks; do not use a per-event admission snapshot. Re-check before accepting done, and let the scheduled check no-op after settlement.
Read namespace.global, errorClass.name and errorClass.memberNameProperty exactly once into plain values; validate and serialize the stored snapshot, never re-read getters for boot.
Hold one cursor per open nesting level instead of copying every member.
Compact consumed queue prefixes during the drain; do not wait for an empty queue.
Bound auxiliary state separately from the primary byte/content budget.
steps: Locate the owning boundary and enumerate every representation and consumer; cite the source ranges recorded in this mechanism.
Install the true pending-call counter, finally release, deduplicated post-macrotask check and independent done admission check at the runtime boundary.
Snapshot binding metadata before validation and boot; keep reply-prefix compaction and per-open-container cursor metering as separate bounds.
Plan concrete instant-burst, unresolved-burst, done-in-same-batch, stateful-getter and sustained-drain controls; retain unexecuted target status.

enforcement.implementation: CPython host owns strict >1024 outstanding-call admission after microtask settlement and before done; validation owns immutable plain metadata; drain/meter owners retain consumed-prefix compaction and O(depth) completion cursors.
enforcement.trust: The observation point must see true outstanding closures, not resolved replies or a stale per-event snapshot; validation and boot use the identical stored metadata.
enforcement.failure: An unresolved-call flood settles worker-exit before wall timeout; metadata getters cannot mutate the accepted boot shape; no byte cap is substituted for the separate call-count bound.
enforcement.exceptions: A settled run makes the scheduled check a no-op, but done independently rejects an over-cap batch before acceptance. O(depth) applies to completion-meter cursors, not the separate O(keys) lossless dictionary-collision set.

mechanisms.title: Incremental Retention Accounting
mechanisms.problem: Retention keeps a linked sequence of strings, head offset, aggregate UTF-8 byte and newline counts; appends evict only oldest code points until both limits hold, so evicted work is charged to earlier appends and total work is linear; reads assemble proportional to retained output. obligations: Reuse the existing terminal command/cwd/wrapping/disclosure from Start for valid explicit background bash/pwsh.
background=true with running=true means launch in progress; acknowledgement retains background but sets running=false and leaves a static command-only card.
After normal acknowledgement show no state dot, exit code, empty-output placeholder or running animation, and retain disclosure state.
Launch failure retains raw args plus error-result presentation; Inspect still exposes complete args and acknowledgement.
Leave final job state/output in the header job panel, completion notices and job_output. Add no subscription, polling, output assembly or jobId/callId index.
Scope is explicit launch only, not timeout promotion or background terminal_send; foreground/persistent Shell and Copy output semantics remain unchanged.
steps: The Client assembly owner forwards original Start background and current call running into the existing terminal component, without a derived job-state parameter.
The component owner preserves command/disclosure across acknowledgement and keeps launch failure on raw-argument/error fallback.
The reviewer compares root/child, acknowledgement/failure and unchanged foreground/persistent/terminal_send paths; inspect final job surfaces separately, never poll from this card.

enforcement.implementation: Source Client assembly/component automatically chooses launch-progress, static command and failure fallback from the original call facts. Target surface binding and UI/assembly execution remain missing; this preserves a source presentation effect without claiming job-state enforcement.
enforcement.trust: Start args and original call running describe launch only. Acknowledgement lacks command exit; independent job panel/notices/reads own final state and output.
enforcement.failure: Launch failure preserves raw args and the error result, not a synthetic completed terminal. Normal acknowledgement remains static and makes no success/failure/liveness claim about the job.
enforcement.exceptions: No reliable jobId-to-callId mapping is added. Timeout promotion and background terminal_send are outside scope; Host/execution/log and foreground/persistent/Copy semantics are unchanged. Constructed assembly cases are not real job-output association proof.

mechanisms.applicability: Apply where a returned background launch and independently owned job state are distinct. If no such surface exists, record that fact and reactivate on introduction; missing job identity is not permission to infer completion.

migration.strategy: Reuse command presentation from raw call facts without introducing a job-state subsystem into the card.
migration.implementation: Pass background/running, preserve command/disclosure and choose static acknowledgement or raw-error fallback; keep independent job owners and explicit-launch scope.
migration.requiredSupport: Real Start/acknowledgement/failure Client assembly, command component and independent job surfaces, with root/child and unchanged-path controls; target UI proof remains missing.

positive.scenario: For root and child explicit background bash/pwsh, open disclosure at Start and observe launch-progress. After normal acknowledgement retain command/cwd/wrapping/open state, with background unchanged and running=false, but no dot/exit/empty-output/animation. Inspect still exposes raw args and acknowledgement; foreground/persistent/terminal_send and Copy remain unchanged.

rejection.scenario: Parsing acknowledgement as a completed-command result must fail absence-of-success controls; retaining running=true must fail the returned-call/static-card control. A card subscription/index/output assembly or generic-JSON-only mutation must fail owner/scope or command-display controls, without pretending acknowledgement contains final output.

recovery.scenario: A launch failure uses the raw-argument plus error-result fallback and does not acquire fake job state. Correct the launch condition and execute a fresh explicit background launch: acknowledgement returns to the static command-only path, while later notices/job_output remain independent. The source specifies fallback, not automatic retry.

mechanisms.limitations: The Tool card never receives final output or authenticates job state. This partially supersedes only the earlier explicit-background Shell generic-body rule, not background terminal_send or timeout promotion. Source constructed assembly regressions are identified data, not live job association. Parent read English8-33; target UI/assembly, linked tests and fresh Chinese equivalence remain unverified.

mechanisms.title: Presentation Eligibility By Facts
mechanisms.problem: Terminal card eligibility applies the same checks to root and nested dispatch calls. parentCallId alone no longer rejects, because nesting does not remove the raw facts the model already consumes; uncertain content keeps conservative generic fallback.
triggers: Root and nested PTC terminal calls have the same raw arguments/result facts but tree position alone rejects the child card.
Persistent/background/error/malformed/missing-head/spill content crosses the eligibility and conservative-fallback boundary.
obligations: Apply the same terminalCardModel checks to root and PTC dispatch calls; parentCallId controls tree placement, not rejection by itself.

Keep tool-error, malformed-input, missing-head and unsupported-result fallback. Persistent Shell is eligible while running and generic when settled; nonzero process exit is result data, not a tool error.

The September Note keeps background calls generic; the October explicit-background bash/pwsh successor uses launch/static command presentation only. Background terminal_send and timeout promotion are not broadened.
A recognized spill notice may follow or replace an exit marker: use expandable generic BashRow/raw Details fallback and never infer successful status from a missing marker.
Reuse browser-safe notice formatSpillNotice/hasSpillNotice and describeOmitted, preserving persisted spelling and result bytes; do not add a UI regex.
Text recognition selects conservative display, not authentication. Other child card metadata restrictions and Host/event/schema/model context remain unchanged.
steps: The shared terminal derivation owner removes only blanket parentCallId rejection and retains each fact-based fallback and persistent-call rule.
The notice owner remains shared by producer and browser Client; the reviewer compares literal historical spelling, unchanged result bytes and notice-only/incomplete-status controls.
The regression owner exercises root/child Rows and Details plus actual PTC spill production; apply the explicit-background successor separately instead of widening every nested card.

enforcement.implementation: Source Client automatically shares terminal eligibility/fallback and browser-safe notice recognition across root/child calls. Target derivation/notice bindings and actual UI/spill execution remain missing; the October explicit-background successor is a scoped rule, not blanket background eligibility.
enforcement.trust: Available raw terminal facts establish presentation eligibility. A parent link or matching notice string cannot authenticate output or establish process success.
enforcement.failure: Unknown/error/malformed/missing-head results and spill notices retain conservative generic output. Settled persistent calls are generic, and an omitted exit marker is not success.
enforcement.exceptions: Nonzero process exit is not tool error. Notice text can be printed by a tool and is not authenticated. Nonterminal child restrictions remain; only explicit background bash/pwsh command display is subsequently superseded.

mechanisms.applicability: Apply to Client-derived terminal cards consuming root/nested raw calls and possible spill text. Record absent surfaces and reactivation facts; do not invent Host metadata or enable unrelated child cards to satisfy presentation.

migration.strategy: Share fact-based terminal derivation and the producer-owned text convention; keep independent child restrictions and the later background scope.
migration.implementation: Remove only tree-position rejection, retain conservative generic paths and exact notice spelling, and delegate explicit-background command state to its successor owner.
migration.requiredSupport: Real root/PTC terminal derivation, browser-safe shared notice owner, persistent/error/malformed/spill controls and actual assembled Client execution; target evidence is outstanding.

positive.scenario: Equivalent supported root/PTC bash/pwsh/terminal_send calls render terminal Rows and selected-child Details while running and on supported settled results. Persistent Shell becomes generic when settled; nonzero process exit remains terminal data. Exercise the October explicit-background launch/static scope separately.

rejection.scenario: Restore blanket parentCallId rejection and the child/root-equivalence control must fail. Enable all nested structured cards or parse around spill suffixes and conservative fallback controls must fail. Produce notice-after-marker and notice-only output, including spoofed notice text: no success/authentication is inferred, and a second drifting UI regex fails shared spelling controls.

recovery.scenario: Tool-error, malformed-input, missing-head and unsupported/spill results keep expandable generic/raw Details fallback. Correct a supported call and rerun through the same root/PTC derivation to recover terminal display without changing log bytes. This is explicit repair plus fallback, not automatic recovery of truncated status.

mechanisms.limitations: Tree placement is independent of terminal eligibility; other child metadata restrictions are unchanged. Notice recognition is not authentication and cannot restore omitted exit status. September background-generic scope has a narrowly cited October explicit-Shell successor, with background terminal_send unchanged. Parent read English8-36 including raw36 and successor8-33; target UI/spill execution and fresh Chinese equivalence remain unverified.

mechanisms.title: Presentation Single Row Escape
mechanisms.problem: Single-row card fields escape newlines at the single-row render site; multi-line fields keep displayText+split; rejecting presenter-level stripping because UI concern belongs at render site
triggers: Newline-bearing commands/descriptions or cwd occupy fields whose terminal layout reserves exactly one logical row.
A tool presenter is about to strip command newlines, or genuine output is about to inherit single-row escaping.
obligations: Use displayInlineText at the single-row render sites for card title, terminal description/cwd and pending $ <command> echo; newline becomes literal \x0a.
Keep genuine captured output and contentText on displayText plus split('\n') so they still occupy real multiline rows.
Preserve raw command shape for every non-row consumer; do not strip newlines in the bash presenter or deliberately wrap the identity title.
steps: The terminal/card render owner identifies the four single-row fields and uses the shared inline escape at those sites only.
The reviewer compares raw presenter values with output/contentText multiline rendering and neighboring row accounting.

The regression owner exercises pending/completed newline-bearing cards through the actual TUI; keep source tmux observations and multilineTerminal fixture as historical evidence, not current target execution.

enforcement.implementation: Source render sites automatically use displayInlineText for one-row fields while multiline result rendering stays unchanged. Target TUI/escape bindings and live proof remain missing; the classification retains source rendering effects, not an implemented target TUI.
enforcement.trust: The render site's reserved field shape selects escaping. Raw command/presenter text remains authoritative; inline display is not a command rewrite.
enforcement.failure: The old structural newline in a one-row title collides with adjacent rows. Source specifies the render correction, not a fallback/quarantine/retry protocol.
enforcement.exceptions: Captured output/contentText legitimately remain multiline. Historical pending/completed tmux proof and the named source fixture do not establish target execution or universal wrapping behavior.

mechanisms.applicability: Apply where row accounting reserves one logical row for identity/meta/command echoes. Record absence of that TUI/layout fact and reactivate when introduced; do not impose inline escaping on genuine multiline output.

migration.strategy: Encode row shape in the rendering owner without altering presenter or command values.
migration.implementation: Bind shared inline escaping to the four reserved-row sites and retain displayText/split for result bodies.
migration.requiredSupport: Real TUI/card layout, shared inline/text escapes, pending/completed newline-bearing fixtures and raw-value/multiline comparators; target live proof is outstanding.

positive.scenario: Render pending and completed cards with newline-bearing title, description, cwd and command echo: literal \x0a keeps each reserved field on one row and adjacent description/output/exit rows intact. Raw commands are unchanged; genuine output/contentText still displays multiple real rows.

rejection.scenario: Restore displayText at a one-row title and observe overlap/accounting failure. Strip newlines in the presenter and raw-value preservation must fail; deliberately wrap the title or inline-escape genuine output and row/body shape controls must fail.

recovery.scenario: Source recovery not applicable: the Note defines single-row rendering, with no independent runtime failure/retry protocol. A target must separately demonstrate rejection-to-repair by correcting the render binding and rerunning the actual TUI, not invent generic fail-loud behavior.

mechanisms.limitations: Inline escaping belongs at reserved-row render sites only, not presenters or multiline output. Historical tmux pending/completed proof and multilineTerminal source assertions are not a current target run. Parent read English8-24 including raw10; no source-test/TUI execution or fresh Chinese equivalence is claimed.

mechanisms.title: Primary Action State Alignment
mechanisms.problem: The single primary pointer control reflects current state and content: empty running draft shows Stop, non-whitespace/attachment shows Send via Queue, owner block keeps Stop because editing/submission are disabled, clearing or successful submit restores Stop; pointer action does not inherit the keyboard Queue/Steer preference; continuable subagents keep independent controls
triggers: An ordinary session remains editable during a running turn and its single pointer control disagrees with the visible draft.
Text/attachment, owner block, clear/submit or keyboard busyEnter preference changes primary-action precedence.
obligations: For an ordinary running session, empty draft shows Stop through session cancellation; non-whitespace text or an attachment switches the same seat to Send through Queue.
Owner-blocked running state keeps Stop even with retained draft because editing/submission are disabled.
Clearing or successfully submitting restores Stop while running; idle keeps Send disabled for empty/unavailable submission.
Pointer Send ignores busyEnter Queue/Steer preference, which remains keyboard-only.
Continuable subagents retain independent Send/Stop; one-shot subagents remain read-only rather than inheriting ordinary-session precedence.
steps: The InputBar owner derives the single ordinary primary seat from running/content/owner block and preserves existing Queue and cancellation callbacks.
The reviewer compares keyboard Steer preference with pointer Queue and verifies idle, block and subagent exceptions.
The regression owner parks a real composed turn, clicks Send with a follow-up, observes Host Queue and Stop after clearing, removes the queued row and cancels through the existing route.

enforcement.implementation: Source InputBar automatically derives action precedence and uses the existing Queue/cancel transports. Target composer/Host bindings and actual pointer/Queue proof remain missing; this preserves source effects without claiming a target UI implementation.
enforcement.trust: Current draft/attachment/running/block facts choose the pointer action; a keyboard preference cannot silently redefine a labeled button.
enforcement.failure: A blocked retained draft cannot be submitted and keeps Stop. Empty/unavailable idle submission is disabled; successful clear/submit restores the running Stop seat.
enforcement.exceptions: Ordinary sessions have one primary seat, not permanent dual controls. Continuable subagents keep independent operations, one-shot remains read-only, and keyboard delivery/cancellation transports are unchanged.

mechanisms.applicability: Apply where an editable running composer has one pointer primary action and separate keyboard delivery preference. Record missing surface facts and reactivate when introduced; retain distinct subagent control models.

migration.strategy: Derive action precedence in the composer owner while reusing transport and preserving keyboard/subagent boundaries.
migration.implementation: Bind content/block/running transitions to Queue Send or Stop; restore Stop after clear/submit and preserve idle/read-only exceptions.
migration.requiredSupport: Real InputBar and Host Queue/cancel entry, attachment/block and keyboard-preference controls, continuable/one-shot subjects and actual pointer interaction; target proof remains outstanding.

positive.scenario: During a real ordinary turn, empty composer shows Stop; text or attachment-only shows Send. With keyboard preference Steer, pointer click still queues through Host, clears the accepted draft and returns Stop. Exercise owner-blocked retained draft, idle empty/unavailable Send and independent continuable/read-only one-shot controls.

rejection.scenario: Restore Stop for the whole running editable draft and pointer submission must instead cancel, failing the follow-up control. Permanent ordinary dual controls and pointer adoption of busyEnter Steer must fail the one-seat/Queue assertions; a blocked retained draft must not be sent.

recovery.scenario: Clear a running text/attachment draft or successfully submit it: the single seat returns to Stop and cancellation still works. Remove the queued follow-up through its existing owner before cancelling the real turn. This is state-transition recovery, not a new retry/delivery protocol.

mechanisms.limitations: An actionable ordinary draft temporarily takes the single seat; simultaneous Stop is not retained until clear/submit/block returns it. Keyboard Queue/Steer, cancellation and subagent controls are unchanged. Source keyless assembled Host Queue proof is historical, not a target run. Parent read English8-32; target UI/Host and Chinese equivalence remain unverified.

mechanisms.title: Process Vs Durable State Separation
mechanisms.problem: Activation is process-local by domain contract. It gets its own live event ({sessionId, goal:{id,revision,activation}}) forwarded as JSON, not persisted into GoalSnapshot or a checkpointed projection, and the non-JSON scoped goal event is not forwarded.
triggers: Web must distinguish armed, active-disarmed and durable-paused goals across restore/fork, running changes or reconnect.
A durable snapshot/checkpoint is about to cache process activation, or an in-flight Remote read could overwrite a newer activation edge.
obligations: Keep process-local activation out of GoalSnapshot and checkpointed projection so restore/fork cannot retain an old armed value.
Expose read-only ctx.goals.get and JSON goal/activation-changed {sessionId,goal:{id,revision,activation}}, with no goal after clear; do not forward scoped goal/changed containing Agent.
GoalBar uses its registrant-private inject-hook source, reading ctx.remote.goals.get and subscribing only while observed; components do not own Remote subscriptions.
Refresh on running-state/connection reset, advance epoch on activation edges to reject stale reads and retain the previous activation during running refresh.

Render active armed as Ongoing Goal/pause, active-disarmed as Inactive Goal/resume and durable paused with resume; resume authority remains in authority-action-propagation, not inferred from UI labels.
steps: The goal/API owners emit the minimal live JSON event and allowlist the read, preserving durable payloads and projection versions.
The slot/inject owner creates the private observed hook source with refresh/epoch/retention behavior; GoalBar consumes it without subscriptions in the component.
The reviewer compares restore/fork, clear, stale HTTP/edge ordering and running/reconnect rendering, and separately checks the user-owned paused-resume authority mechanism.

enforcement.implementation: Source goal/API/hook owners automatically keep activation live-only, forward JSON and fence asynchronous reads. Target domain/Remote/source bindings and actual UI/restore execution remain missing; mode preserves those effects rather than claiming the Skill implements them.
enforcement.trust: Current process activation and event epoch are authoritative for live rendering; durable status is a different fact. JSON allowlisting excludes scoped Agent payloads.
enforcement.failure: A stale read cannot overwrite a newer edge and running refresh retains the last activation. Clear yields no goal; restore/fork does not inherit checkpointed armed state.
enforcement.exceptions: Durable paused still exposes user resume, active-disarmed exposes resume and blocked continuation remains governed by the domain/tool authority. No durable format/projection version change or component-owned subscription is introduced.

mechanisms.applicability: Apply where process-local activation and durable goal status are separate and clients read asynchronously. Record absent domain/Remote facts and reactivate on introduction; a missing live-data channel is an open applicable effect gap.

migration.strategy: Keep process facts in the domain/live hook channel, wire only JSON and reject stale read replacement.
migration.implementation: Bind read-only get, minimal activation events and private observed source to GoalBar, without persisting activation or bypassing paused-resume authority.
migration.requiredSupport: Real goal activation, JSON Remote allowlist, observed hook source/epoch, restore/fork/reconnect and paused-authority controls; target effect execution remains outstanding.

positive.scenario: Create/start/resume/clear a goal: JSON activation events retain exact id/revision or no goal, and read-only get agrees. Armed active renders Ongoing Goal/pause, disarmed active renders Inactive Goal/resume and durable paused offers user resume. Restore/fork does not retain a prior process armed value.

rejection.scenario: Persist activation in GoalSnapshot or the checkpointed projection and restore/fork must expose stale armed state, failing the live-only control. Forward scoped goal/changed with Agent and JSON-wire validation must fail. Return an old HTTP activation after a newer edge: removing the epoch guard must fail current-state preservation.

recovery.scenario: During running refresh retain prior activation until the read resolves; on connection reset refresh through the observed private source. A newer activation edge invalidates stale reads and clear removes the goal. Separately exercise user-owned paused resume at the authority mechanism; refresh never grants the model that authority.

mechanisms.limitations: Activation must not survive restore/fork in durable state; labels cannot decide resume authority. Private observed hook owns subscription/refresh, and durable goal payload/projection versions stay unchanged. Parent read English8-36 including raw16; target goal/Remote/UI/source tests and fresh Chinese equivalence remain unverified.

mechanisms.title: Producer Owned Serialization Normalization
mechanisms.problem: The store bridge converts a grant credential to its JSON image (explicit undefined members dropped, undefined array entries null), matching JSON.stringify semantics, while foreign values pass through so the strict store still fails loud; JSON round-trip rejected because it also nulls non-finite numbers and invokes toJSON; validator not relaxed
triggers: A change, migration, incident or review concerns producer owned serialization normalization.
A consumer would duplicate, bypass or re-derive the rule instead of using its owner.

The source failure mode is reachable: The store bridge converts a grant credential to its JSON image (explicit undefined members dropped, undefined array entries null), matching JSON.stringify semantics, while foreign…
obligations: Producer converts its library's grant credential to a JSON image: drop explicitly-undefined members of plain objects and render undefined array entries as null, matching JSON.stringify semantics.
Pass non-finite numbers and foreign-prototype objects through untouched so the shared strict store still refuses a genuinely unstorable value; do not relax that validator.

Do not use JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...)) or another general round-trip that nulls non-finite numbers or invokes toJSON; normalization belongs to the producer that knows the library idiom, not the shared byte-faithful store.
Accept the one-way read consequence: a member explicitly undefined at write time is absent on read and indistinguishable from absence for property access.
steps: Producer auth owner implements the local JSON-image conversion at the credential→grant payload boundary, leaving foreign values and the store validator alone.
Reviewer checks explicit-undefined member/array-hole handling, non-finite/foreign-prototype pass-through and absence of toJSON invocation.
Regression owner writes the real Copilot-shaped grant through the actual credential provider and separately commits a Date-valued member to assert the store refusal reaches the caller.

enforcement.implementation: Source producer automatically stores the JSON image while the strict shared store keeps rejecting unrepresentable values. Target credential producer/store bindings and actual write/refusal proof remain missing.
enforcement.trust: The producer owns its library's local serialization idiom; the shared store owns byte-faithful persistence and refusal.
enforcement.failure: A genuinely unstorable member such as Date must fail loud at the store and reach the caller; it must not be silently reshaped by the bridge or validator.
enforcement.exceptions: Explicit-undefined plain-object members and undefined array entries are the only normalization; NaN/Infinity and toJSON-bearing values keep their own semantics. Read-back lacks dropped members indistinguishably from absence.

mechanisms.applicability: Apply when the same trigger, effect and trust boundary exist. Parameterize component names, paths, limits and platform spellings; do not apply as a slogan when the trigger is absent.

migration.strategy: Owner-first migration: make the owning boundary authoritative, migrate every consumer, retain only source-mandated compatibility, and add a negative control.
migration.implementation: Bind the equivalent credential producer's own JSON-image conversion, keeping the shared store strict and byte-faithful; do not widen the store to accommodate one library's idiom.
migration.requiredSupport: Real credential provider/store with an optional-member grant, an array hole and a deliberately unstorable Date control. Missing target binding is not a satisfied inactive disposition.

positive.scenario: Commit a Copilot-shaped grant with explicit undefined member, nested drop and array hole through the real LocalCredentialProvider: stored payload is the JSON image (members absent, hole null), property reads of optional members behave as before.

rejection.scenario: Replace the bridge with JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(credential)): a NaN/Infinity member becomes null or a toJSON method runs, silently reshaping values the strict validator exists to refuse. Relaxing the store validator is a separate rejected widening.

recovery.scenario: Commit a credential carrying a Date-valued member through toRecord: the strict store's refusal reaches the caller and no JSON image is stored. Correcting the producer's unrepresentable value and retrying stores successfully; the source defines no automatic recovery for the refused payload.

mechanisms.limitations: English8-30 read. Normalization is one-way and producer-local; non-finite/toJSON and foreign-prototype values are not normalized, and the store validator is not relaxed. Source testing uses the real provider plus a Date refusal control. Target producer/store binding and runtime proof missing; prior Chinese provenance historical, scenarios planned.

mechanisms.title: Projection Separation
mechanisms.problem: The human transcript projects raw log order and never consults model surface order; model-only replacement copies stay out, and a compaction marker reports a boundary instead of erasing history.
triggers: A change, migration, incident or review concerns Projection Separation.
A consumer would duplicate, bypass or re-derive the rule instead of using its owner.

The source failure mode is reachable: The human transcript projects raw log order and never consults model surface order; model-only replacement copies stay out, and a compaction marker reports a boundary instead of erasing history.
obligations: Project the raw window in durable log order: every append-origin surface event at its own log position plus one compaction marker per landed checkpoint, never consulting model surface order.
Keep model-only replacement copies (pruned tool/result, regenerated assistant/message) out of the human transcript; everything that must send exactly the model view keeps reading the surface.

Report a landed compaction as a boundary at its flow position, retaining the shadowed conversation on the human side; source marker count/token text from the cited structured compaction/summary event, not the framed checkpoint instruction payload or settlement presentation text.

Pair a successful named /compact row only with the exactly matching unique loaded summaryEventSeq; keep rejection/no-history/cancellation/failure as complete generic command rows and automatic compaction as its standalone marker.

Keep node order seq-monotonic: log-only command pairs splice by seq, Session-owned interrupted frozen nodes merge by fractional seq, and a checkpoint citing a range outside the page renders without logging or a degraded flag.
steps: Transcript projection owner builds from append-origin log events and landed checkpoint declarations, retaining surface readers only where the model view is required.
Reviewer checks marker provenance (structured summary event), unique successful command reference and page-cut soft-fall, rejecting adjacency pairing or presentation-text parsing.

Regression owner replays a real manual compaction lifecycle and a window missing the summary event, asserting log-order retention, marker soft-fall then resolution, and unchanged identity for unchanged nodes.

enforcement.implementation: Source transcript adapter automatically projects append-origin log order and marker boundaries without a surface fold. Target adapter/checkpoint/command bindings and actual browser replay proof remain missing.
enforcement.trust: The durable log and the cited structured summary event own human ordering and marker facts; the model surface owns only what the model sees.
enforcement.failure: A missing summary event leaves marker count/token fields unavailable rather than throwing or logging; no foldDegraded sentinel exists to describe a fold that no longer runs.
enforcement.exceptions: A window whose checkpoint cites an outside range has nothing to resolve; older persisted logs without the optional command reference keep the former two-row soft-fall with no migration. Model-only replacements mark no boundary.

mechanisms.applicability: Apply when the same trigger, effect and trust boundary exist. Parameterize component names, paths, limits and platform spellings; do not apply as a slogan when the trigger is absent.

migration.strategy: Owner-first migration: make the owning boundary authoritative, migrate every consumer, retain only source-mandated compatibility, and add a negative control.
migration.implementation: Project the target conversation from its durable append-origin log and checkpoint declarations, removing any surface-order fold or degraded padding while keeping a separate exact model-view reader.
migration.requiredSupport: Durable log/checkpoint/command-reference contracts plus real browser replay with a recorded manual compaction and a summary event outside the page. Missing target binding is not a satisfied inactive disposition.

positive.scenario: Replay a recorded manual compaction over a turn: the prompt and full tool output remain on screen in log order, exactly one compact row reports scale after them, its disclosure opens the exact structured summary, and unchanged nodes keep identity across append/chunk storms.

rejection.scenario: Reintroduce the surface-order fold or host-side empty-node filtering: shadowed history collapses into one dim row, or a model-only pruned tool/result/regenerated assistant copy appears as a boundary. Assert the host state still retains the log and the transcript does not.

recovery.scenario: Load a window whose checkpoint cites a compaction/summary event outside the page: marker renders with unavailable count/token fields and nothing is logged or reordered; a later page supplying that event resolves the fields. Pair a command with missing/ambiguous/non-matching sourceEventSeq and observe no stolen checkpoint.

mechanisms.limitations: English8-79/raw16,24 read in the preceding batch; this batch adds the recovery/soft-fall and command-scope precision. Projection is linear in window length, not bounded by compaction, and unchanged arrays/nodes retain identity. Target adapter/command/browser replay and compiler purity proof missing; prior Chinese provenance historical, scenarios planned.

mechanisms.title: Prompt Fact Ownership
mechanisms.problem: Prompt section names the implementation checkout and states checkout vs cwd are separate values that may differ, forbids inference and directs pwd; rejects the false blanket 'never equal' because meta mode intentionally coincides; global source fact must not absorb session-owned cwd
triggers: The launcher-global implementation checkout could be mistaken for the session's current working directory.
Prompt construction changes source ownership/order or falsely says checkout and cwd can never coincide.
obligations: Identify harness:source as the DeepSeek Harness implementation checkout, useful for inspecting/extending DSH itself.
State checkout location and current working directory are separate values that may differ; prohibit inferring cwd from checkout and direct the model to pwd.
Preserve launcher-global checkout derivation and first-party order-900 immediately after identity; do not put session-owned cwd into that global section.
Remain truthful when dsh meta deliberately makes both values equal; reject blanket never-equal wording without removing checkout purpose.
steps: The launcher/prompt owner retains checkout derivation and identity/source ordering while stating ownership and the pwd instruction.
The reviewer checks ordinary unrelated-workspace and meta-equal worlds, keeping per-session cwd out of the global source fact.
The evidence owner separates source text/order unit pins, assembled keyless PTY header and recorded-model TUI replay; actual target answers require their own observed command/output.

enforcement.implementation: Source prompt construction automatically emits the owned checkout section/order and its explicit instruction. That does not deterministically enforce model answers or pwd use. Target prompt-construction binding and actual model/PTY observations remain missing.
enforcement.trust: Launcher checkout and session cwd are independently owned facts. pwd can establish cwd; checkout presence or a replay fixture cannot authenticate a future model answer.
enforcement.failure: The original ambiguous source wording can induce a wrong cwd answer. The Note defines a construction correction, not a runtime rejection/fail-loud/retry protocol for model noncompliance.
enforcement.exceptions: dsh meta intentionally coincides. Text/order tests and keyless header inspection prove construction, while the recorded DeepSeekV4 replay proves that recorded case only; none guarantees all future model compliance.

mechanisms.applicability: Apply where launcher-global implementation location and per-session workdir coexist in prompts. Record absent checkout/prompt ownership and reactivate when introduced; never invent a false always-unequal rule.

migration.strategy: Preserve independently owned facts and truthful instructions without merging global and session state.
migration.implementation: Bind accurate checkout purpose, separate-values/pwd wording and stable order; verify actual prompt assembly separately from model behavior.
migration.requiredSupport: Real launcher prompt assembly, unrelated/equal-meta session facts, assembled request/PTY inspection and separately observed model/tool behavior; target construction and compliance proof remain missing.

positive.scenario: Assemble identity then order-900 harness:source with an implementation checkout distinct from cwd and with an equal dsh meta world. Both carry accurate separate-values/purpose/pwd wording without a global cwd value. Separately observe actual pwd and answer in a target session; do not substitute a literal text pin for that behavior.

rejection.scenario: Never-equal wording must fail the meta-equal truth control; merging cwd into launcher-global source must fail session-ownership isolation. Removing checkout purpose must fail unrelated-launcher self-inspection context. Treating a recorded model replay as universal output enforcement must fail the evidence-scope review.
